In the HBO show 《Last Week Tonight》, in an episode aired on Sunday, Oliver publicly attacked his incoming, MAGA-aligned boss, accusing him of playing a key role in kicking Stephen Colbert off the television screen.

The brilliance of this mockery is that while assuring Ellison that he would "never make fun of" him, Oliver had already done so—and the entire backdrop of the segment was an examination of UnitedHealthcare's operations.

The comedian began by recounting the story of Kate Weissman: a cancer patient who, despite most of her Harvard-affiliated attending physicians recommending treatment, was denied coverage by UnitedHealthcare for a life-saving procedure. In the end, Weissman's parents paid out of pocket, covering her $95,000 (approximately HK$730,000) medical expenses.

Oliver said: "Whether or not you have wealthy parents should never be a prerequisite for receiving urgently needed medical care," at which point Ellison's photo popped up on screen. "Even if that seems to be the rule that got you put in charge of HBO."

Oliver said: "Oh right, my future boss has a real sugar daddy behind him," at which point Ellison's photo zoomed in, with that of his father—billionaire Oracle CEO Larry Ellison—added alongside.

According to The New York Times, Paramount reached a deal on Monday, clearing the "last major hurdle" to acquiring Warner Bros. Discovery—the parent company of HBO, which is the platform on which 《Last Week Tonight》 airs.

HBO will be merged into Paramount's larger media empire, which already includes the CBS television network and is currently being revamped under the leadership of David Ellison.

Oliver, dripping with sarcasm, shifted his tone to a mock-sincere register: "I want to be clear—I have tremendous respect for this. And I absolutely will not make fun of you for it. Not like that annoying Stephen Colbert."
